title: The Emergency
subtitle: A Newspaper With a Blank Column
intro: The Emergency. A democracy suspended in the name of stability; the debate over civil liberty, federalism and memory remains live.
lede: A 4:07 film in 8 scenes and 42 shots, built from 8 procedural sets, 40 sourced lines and 7 authored transitions. Every frame rendered on free GitHub Actions hardware.

stats.label: sourced lines
stats.note: every line carries a source id

cut.heading: 42 shots across 8 scenes.
cut.body: The final cut runs 4:07 at 24 fps; the average shot is 5.9 seconds. 35 of the 42 joins are hard cuts. The other 7 are authored transitions (paper wipe, page turn, iris, dip). The scene list below is generated from the release timeline, not the storyboard.

motion.heading: The edit has a grammar.
motion.body: The grammar is paper-ledger. The signature moves are listed below. Transition counts come from the final edit manifest.
signature: blank-column reveal: the censored space moves before the camera does
page-turn wipe: a printed edge carries the next set in
stamp match: a rubber stamp lands where the last shot cut
register rule: horizontal ruling lines become cell bars
lamp iris: a reading lamp closes to a circle on the page
paper stack: sheets rise into frame to bury the object

families.name: Paper wipe
families.use: A printed edge carries the next set into frame.

families.name: Page turn
families.use: A page turns and the next set arrives on its back.

families.name: Iris
families.use: A lamp or valve closes to a circle, moving the eye to the next object.

families.name: Dip
families.use: A held gap between two arguments.

families.name: Hard cut
families.use: The default join. Used where softening would weaken the argument.

items.title: Forty-second Amendment of the Constitution of India

pipeline.heading: Every frame is assembled on GitHub.
pipeline.body: Blender, Piper, Chromium and ffmpeg run on a free Ubuntu CPU runner. The owner's machine writes the code; it does not render the film. The pipeline is public, repeatable and allowed to fail loudly.

items.title: Source lock
items.body: The storyboard is a JSON contract. Every narration line names a source. The validator refuses unsourced lines, missing shots and filler before a runner is allowed to render.

items.title: Procedural sets
items.body: Blender 4.2 builds the film's sets as still plates. No stock images.

items.title: Narration
items.body: Piper reads the script locally with en_US-lessac-medium. No cloud narration, no per-word billing, no API key in the repository.

items.title: Camera and type
items.body: Chromium drives the timeline frame by frame: push-ins, pans, match cuts, mask wipes, impact cards and captions. The camera is code, so every frame is repeatable.

items.title: Score and master
items.body: ffmpeg synthesises the score, mixes the narration, burns the SRT into the master and encodes the MP4.

items.title: Free CI
items.body: The render runs on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu CPU. No GPU. No paid runner. The owner's machine writes the code; it does not render the film.

record.heading: What the record shows.
record.body: Each entry is taken from the release itself: the timeline, the edit manifest and the independent QC report. A dossier that only shows the final cut is a portfolio, not a process.

items.title: Source lock
items.body: 40 narration lines across 5 sources. Every line in the final timeline resolves to a source in the release metadata; the validator refuses a line without one.

items.title: Final cut
items.body: 8 scenes, 42 shots, 4:07. Average shot 5.9s. 35 hard cuts and 7 authored transitions.

items.title: Independent QC
items.body: Passed: -1.8 dBTP wanted no higher than -1; I -13.5 LUFS wanted -16.5 to -11; median 45.9 dB wanted at least 36 dB, worst 42.1 dB at S01; 73 cues in emergency-1975.srt; median edge/interior 1.27 wanted at most 1.75.

items.title: Release
items.body: Release film-emergency-1975-final-28 carries the 1080 master, SRT, thumbnail, timeline, edit manifest and script. The site deploys only the 720 preview.

build.heading: The render is public.
build.body: Recent Film pipeline runs, read from the public GitHub API. The workflow log is part of the record.

credits.heading: Who did what.
credits.body: The same free, local toolchain on every film: no paid API, no GPU and no stock footage.
rules: Every narration line carries a source id. The render fails if a line, shot or source is missing.
No number on screen without a source or an explicit attribution.
No stock footage. Every set is procedural.
No paid API keys. The pipeline runs on free CI.
If the edit is weak, the render does not ship.
credits.quote: “If the edit is weak, the render does not ship.”

scenes.title: The object
scenes.purpose: Open on one thing the film can hold, then land the title without a lecture.

narration.text: The Delhi edition of the Indian Express carried a blank editorial on 28 June.
The Financial Express reproduced Rabindranath Tagore's poem Where the mind is without fear in large type.
More than 100,000 political opponents, journalists and dissenters were imprisoned.
The central government imposed strict censorship on radio, television and newspapers during this period.
All publications were subjected to substantial censorship by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.

scenes.title: The order
scenes.purpose: Show the decision, who made it, and the words it was made in.

narration.text: West Bengal Chief Minister Siddhartha Shankar Ray proposed that the prime minister impose an internal emergency.
Indira Gandhi requested President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed to proclaim a state of emergency later that day.
On 25 June 1975, Ahmed declared a State of Emergency under Article 352(1), citing internal disorder.
When existing laws seemed too slow, she had the President issue Ordinances, bypassing Parliament and ruling by decree.
The Emergency remained in effect until 21 March 1977.

scenes.title: The machine
scenes.purpose: Explain how the decision reached ordinary life: the law, the police, the press.

narration.text: The government introduced press censorship, postponed elections and banned strikes and rallies.
Within three hours, the electricity to every major newspaper was cut.
Police forces were empowered to make warrantless searches and arrests.
Under MISA, 34,988 people were arrested; under DISIR, 75,818.
The Government placed thousands of protestors and strike leaders under preventive detention.

scenes.title: The cost
scenes.purpose: Count what it took, in the terms the record uses, without inventing a figure.

narration.text: Amnesty International recorded 140,000 arrests without trial during the twenty months of the Emergency.
Teenagers faced imprisonment, with one sixteen-year-old detained for over eleven months.
The sterilization program reached 8.3 million procedures in 1976 and 1977, mostly forced.
Rajan from the Regional Engineering College suffered torture and died while in police custody.
The commission found that vagabonds and beggars were forced into sterilization clinics by Youth Congress workers and the police.

scenes.title: The turn
scenes.purpose: Find the moment the order broke: the election, the release, the first page printed again.

narration.text: Mrs Indira Gandhi called elections for March and released all political prisoners on 23 January 1977.
The Janata party won a sweeping victory on 23 March, securing 43.2% of the popular vote.
The Janata Party manifesto promised to restore the Constitution to its pre-Emergency condition.
Morarji Desai became the first non-Congress prime minister after the party defeated the Congress (R) in 1977.
The Janata alliance claimed the elections were India's last chance to choose between democracy and dictatorship.

scenes.title: The argument
scenes.purpose: Put the dispute on the table: who defended it, who fought it, and on what ground.

narration.text: Indira Gandhi defended the emergency as essential for national security despite offering apologies for abuses.
Critics condemned her authoritarian rule and cult of personality during the Emergency period.
The 42nd Amendment faced widespread criticism for clamping down on civil liberties and human rights.
The amendment deprived citizens of direct access to the Supreme Court except for fundamental rights violations.
In a seven-to-six decision, the Supreme Court restricted Parliament's power to alter the Constitution's basic structure.

scenes.title: The record
scenes.purpose: Show what was written down, and what the writing left out.

narration.text: The Shah Commission began hearing oral evidence on 29 September 1977.
It found that the Maintenance of Internal Security Act and Defence of India Rules were abused against political opponents.
The final report, issued on 6 August 1978, covered prison conditions, torture, and family planning atrocities.
Critics later argued that the commission confused investigation with inquiry.
The commission missed its initial 31 December 1977 deadline and received an extension to 30 June 1978.

scenes.title: The return
scenes.purpose: Return to the opening object: what survived, what was withdrawn, what is still on the record.

narration.text: Parliament passed an act on 8 May 1979 establishing two special courts.
Indira Gandhi returned to power in January 1980 after a landslide election victory.
The Supreme Court found the special courts were not legally constituted, so no trials were held.
Indira Gandhi attempted to recall copies of the Shah Commission report wherever possible.
The Indian Express carried a blank editorial on 28 June during the Emergency.
